title: Text, data & visual mining
source: Session 4 handout (DDM 26/27) – Coca-Cola Social Hub, Boeing reputation case, crypto sentiment study, Dash Hudson & YouScan, Brand24 team activity
tagline: Most marketing data is unstructured – posts, reviews, images. Text, data and visual mining (TDVM) turn it into patterns, predictions and sentiment you can act on. You will rarely mine yourself, but you must know which algorithm does what and how to read the output.
goals: define **text mining, data mining, predictive analytics, social listening, sentiment analysis and visual mining**
order the **text-mining steps** from tokenization to topic modelling
match a business problem to a **data-mining algorithm**
describe the **social listening process** and who does each step

sections.heading: Six methods at a glance
sections.lead: Every minute Coca-Cola is mentioned more than 30 times on social media in English alone – its Social Hub monitors and analyses these posts in real time for marketers worldwide.

items.label: Text mining
items.text: Treatment of unstructured text information; e.g. automatic grouping of similar texts.

items.label: Data mining
items.text: Exploration and analysis of data to uncover meaningful patterns or rules.

items.label: Predictive analytics
items.text: Predicts future outcomes from historical data with statistical modelling, data mining and machine learning.

items.label: Social listening
items.text: Identifying and assessing what is being said about a company, person, product or brand online.

items.label: Sentiment analysis
items.text: Analysing online text to determine its emotional tone – positive, negative or neutral; how the author feels about a topic.

items.label: Visual mining
items.text: Extracting trends, patterns and insights from visual data with data mining, computer vision and visualisation.

blocks.text: Social listening asks **what** is said (volume, reach, topics); sentiment analysis asks **how** it is said (tone). Listening collects, sentiment evaluates.

sections.heading: Text mining: from raw text to meaning

steps.label: Tokenization
steps.text: Text divided into smaller units called **tokens** (words, characters)

steps.label: Stemming / lemmatization
steps.text: Words reduced to their root or base form (“buying”, “bought” → “buy”)

steps.label: TF-IDF
steps.text: Statistical weight of a term: frequent in this document, rare across all documents = important

steps.label: Named entity recognition (NER)
steps.text: Identify and classify entities – names, brands, locations

steps.label: Opinion mining / sentiment analysis
steps.text: Classify text as positive, negative or neutral

steps.label: Topic modelling & text classification
steps.text: Extract hidden topics; assign predefined labels or categories

blocks.title: Social listening process
blocks.note: Strategy (objectives) and the human response stay in house; collection, analysis and monitoring run on platforms such as Brand24.

sides.label: Neutral
points: Lack of emotion and bias – objective statements

blocks.title: Applications
items: Brand reputation management and monitoring – e.g. **Boeing** after the China Eastern 737-800 crash: sentiment and reputation score track the damage
Customer research and feedback; customer service and support
Market research for decision-making; social media, financial and political analysis
Prediction: social-media sentiment (measured 3× per day) predicted short-term **cryptocurrency prices** with regression, boosting and neural networks – the final model was profitable

blocks.name: Sentiment ratio (Brand24 activity)
blocks.formula: Sentiment ratio = positive mentions / negative mentions
blocks.note: Also compare **volume of mentions** and **social vs. non-social reach** – and ask which events (launches, outages, news) drove the numbers in the period.

blocks.title: Two brands over 30 days
blocks.question: Which brand has the better sentiment?
steps: Nova has more buzz (volume), Orbit the better tone
blocks.result: Orbit has the higher sentiment ratio (4.5 vs. 2.0) despite fewer mentions – volume measures buzz, not tone.

items.label: Dash Hudson – Vision AI
items.text: Learning since 2016; goes beyond topics, hashtags and keywords to surface **visual trends** and community sentiment across social media.

items.label: YouScan – image recognition
items.text: Over half of monitored posts are images; Visual Insights find new use cases, influencers and measure the impact of offline campaigns.

blocks.title: Takeaways
items: Huge untapped potential: **above 80 %** of visual imagery (photos, videos) is not analysed
Draws on multimedia, computer vision and pattern recognition
Excellent way to pick up emerging trends early and keep an eye on competitors
Empowers better decisions for the marketer

blocks.title: Why TDVM matters for data-driven marketing
blocks.text: Extract insights from large amounts of textual, numerical and visual information → understand sentiments, preferences and behaviour **at scale** → targeted, personalised strategies, optimised campaigns and better customer experience.

recap: Text mining handles unstructured text; data mining finds patterns; predictive analytics forecasts; social listening = what is said; sentiment = how it is said; visual mining = images and video.
Text pipeline: **tokenization → stop words → stemming/lemmatization → TF-IDF → NER / sentiment / topic modelling**.
Classification predicts categories, regression continuous values, clustering groups, association rules find “bought together”, anomaly detection finds fraud.
Social listening: objectives (in house) → collection → analysis → insights (tools) → engagement (in house) → monitoring.
**Sentiment ratio = positive / negative mentions**; > 1 = more positive. Volume ≠ tone.
Over 80 % of visual data is untapped – visual mining spots trends and competitors early.
exam: T/F or MC on definitions and on what each text-mining step does (e.g. “Stemming removes words without meaning” → false, that is stop-word removal).
Small calculation: sentiment ratio of two brands and interpretation alongside volume and reach.
Match algorithms to examples (fraud → anomaly detection; churn yes/no → classification).
traps: A sentiment ratio **below 1** means more **negative** mentions.
Regression in data mining predicts continuous values; classification predicts classes – don't swap them.
Innovations in visual mining tools are not the goal – the insight for decisions is.
